story:
The vigil around the bones of Modernagrav is kept by dead beasts: mammoths decaying on their feet, great cats and serpents with the light showing through them, and howlers that should have rotted long ago. Not all the howlers on the island are dead. In the far north-east, out past Basilius's hall, a pack of living ones hunts, and their leader is a big grey howler the dwarves of the post call Rolf.

The name is a dwarf's joke. The Remnants say the living howlers are the descendants of the ones in the vigil, the ones that did not walk in to the bones when the others did, a long time ago; that some of the pack stayed out, and lived, and had pups, and that their pups have been living on the island's far edge ever since, as far from the bones as the island goes. The dwarves gave the leader a man's name, the commonest in Midgard, because, Orri of Hagall wrote, he behaves like a man who has decided not to go to a funeral: he stays away, and makes a great deal of noise about it.

He howls at night. The vigil does not answer. The morvalt of Basilius's hall, who live closest, hate the sound, and the dwarves say Hoden once went out with a cord to take the pack as dogs for the hall, because a king should have hounds, and came back with the cord and no dogs, and that Rolf's pack howled outside the hall every night for a season afterwards.

Rolf hunts alone when he hunts big. The pack runs a little way off, and does not run to him, and the dwarves think that is the howlers' way: the leader kills, and the pack eats after. A stranger who meets Rolf in the north-east meets one howler. Orri wrote that the stranger had better hope it stays one, and that the pack has excellent hearing.
legend: Rolf is a level 50 named howler in the far north-east of Modernagrav, about 1,800 from Basilius's hall, with a pack of five howlers (48-50) about a thousand units away. He has no faction, so he never calls the pack in, but if you fight near them they'll see it and join on their own. Pull him away from the pack (west, toward the middle of the island, not east toward Basilius). No abilities, not CC-immune: an easy named for a small group or a strong pet class. Keep well clear of Basilius's hall: the king's aggro range is 800 and his whole pack comes with him.

bookPage: From the slates of Orri of Hagall: there is a living howler in the north-east, a big grey one, and I have heard him howl on still nights from the post, though it is a long way. The vigil round the bones has howlers in it, dead, standing with the mammoths, facing in. When the grey one howls they do not turn their heads. But once, a winter ago, I watched one of the dead howlers at the edge of the vigil, and when the howl came its ear moved. Only the one ear. I wrote it down and did not break that slate.
